item.description:
• Your road on the street. A road you import is lined up with the streets of OpenStreetMap on your Mac, so in 3D it lies on the asphalt and follows every hairpin, where it used to cut across bends. You are asked once, as for the finer heights, and only the 4 km map squares the road passes through are sent. A road you imported before: its … menu › Line up with the streets.
  • Your marker where the gradient is. The marker, the climb signs and the road's colours now sit where the trainer changes, not tens of metres away on a long road.
  • The camera stays above ground. Starting partway up a road could leave the 3D view looking at the ground from a few metres, with no road; it now flies to you and follows only once the map has caught up.
  • Finer heights for roads in France, Switzerland and Austria. The laser surveys of IGN, swisstopo and BEV join North Rhine-Westphalia's: a road you import there can ride on heights every 20 m, so a short ramp is as steep as it is. As before, Anifora asks first, sends only the 4 km map squares the road passes through, and never the road or a ride.
  • Galleries ridden straight. Avalanche galleries and covered roads join bridges and tunnels: where the laser saw the slope over the roof, the road is ridden straight between its ends.

• The road no longer flickers in 3D. The coloured road used to be redrawn every few metres of riding, and it blinked all the time at speed. It is now drawn once and stays put.
  • You stay in the middle of the picture. The camera follows your marker at every distance, Close, Mid or Far, until you move the map yourself. It used to aim a little up the road, and on roads along a hillside that could leave you at the bottom edge or off the screen.
  • One marker for you. A dot on the road marks where you are, drawn over trees and houses. It replaces the light on the road and the beacon over it, which could not be switched off.
  • Chevrons are off. Menu › Chevrons on the road brings them back, without the pulse.
  • Updates wait for you. When an update is ready as Anifora opens, the card waits until you press Restart Now (or Later). It no longer restarts by itself after ten seconds.

• The 3D world no longer eats memory. Left on the start line (or paused) it grew by about 30 MB a second — on one Mac to 95 GB, until macOS paused every app. It now stays flat, and a ride uses about half the memory it did.
  • A safety net for the map. Anifora watches its own memory: if Apple's map ever runs away with it, the map is closed and the ride carries on in the classic screen, trainer and recording untouched. A banner says so; the map is back the next time Anifora opens.
  • Beta reports. While Anifora is in beta it tells the developer how it ran — errors, crashes, memory, its own log — so problems on your Mac get found without you having to report them. Never a ride, a heart rate or your name, never during a ride, and only after you have seen the note saying so. Settings (⌘,) switches it off and shows what is waiting to go.
